title: Lava that is older than it looks
text: The Black Mountain Basalt in the El Paso Mountains was once thought to be Pleistocene in age, but it was shown to be Miocene. Four potassium-argon ages range from 15.1 to 17.9 million years. The basalt erupted mostly from east-west fissures, which reflects north-south extension between the Mojave Desert block and the southwestern Basin and Range. It is chemically distinctive, a potassium-poor high-alumina basalt.

s1.title: Geologic map of the El Paso Mountains Wilderness Study Area, Kern County, California (MF-1827)
s1.quote: The Black Mountain Basalt, formerly considered to be Pleistocene in age, is determined to be Miocene on the basis of its stratigraphic relations with the Ricardo Formation; this age assignment is confirmed by four potassium-argon ages ranging from 15.1±0.5 m.y. to 17.9±1.6 m.y. The Black Mountain Basalt is chemically distinctive, consisting of potassium-poor high-alumina basalt ... The basalt was erupted mostly from east-west fissures, reflecting north-south extension between the Mojave Desert block and southwestern Basin and Range during early and middle Miocene time.
